title: How do we find 104 squared and 37 squared with the square of a sum?
description: Each number is split into two parts, and the square of a sum gives its square in three pieces. Both answers are checked by multiplying in a different way.
teaching_notes: One idea: split the number into a round number and a small number, then use the square of a sum. Same method as the square of three j plus two k in your book.

source: Use the square of a sum to find the values of 104² and 37². (Hint: split 104 and 37 into sums of numbers whose squares are easy to compute.)
video_script.why: The child has expanded the square of a sum with letters. Here the two terms are numbers.
video_script.substitution: Split each number into a round number and a small number, put them in the square of a sum, add the three pieces, and check by multiplying another way.
video_script.anchor: one hundred four and thirty seven, each split into two parts
video_script.payoff_line: A round number and a small number make the squares quick

final_answer.spoken: one hundred four squared is ten thousand eight hundred sixteen, and thirty seven squared is one thousand three hundred sixty nine

video_script.design: One idea: split into a round number and a small number, then use the square of a sum. Uses the method of the three j plus two k video. Each answer is checked by multiplying another way.

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Step one, split one hundred four as one hundred plus four.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>The square of one hundred is ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Twice one hundred times four is eight hundred.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The square of four is sixteen.
<bookmark mark='tot'/>The total is ten thousand eight hundred sixteen.

beats.colours: each piece in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Step two, split thirty seven as thirty plus seven.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>The square of thirty is nine hundred.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Twice thirty times seven is four hundred twenty.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The square of seven is forty nine.
<bookmark mark='tot'/>The total is one thousand three hundred sixty nine.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Step three, check by multiplying in another way.
One hundred four times one hundred four is ten thousand four hundred, plus four hundred sixteen.
<bookmark mark='b'/>That is ten thousand eight hundred sixteen.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Thirty seven times forty is one thousand four hundred eighty.
Take away thirty seven times three, which is one hundred eleven.
<bookmark mark='d'/>That leaves one thousand three hundred sixty nine.
